title: AUDIT: NetworkPolicy selects the client and denies all egress (looks like DNS, is NetworkPolicy)
symptom: Client pod ca1-client cannot resolve or reach service ca1-server-svc even though the server pod exists.

groundTruth.mechanism: NetworkPolicy ca1-deny-egress selects the client (app=ca1-client) and lists policyTypes:[Egress] with no egress rules, denying ALL egress from the client including DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to CoreDNS. This is NOT a client DNS override; the pod uses ClusterFirst DNS with no dnsConfig.
groundTruth.scope: traffic involving this case's client/server pods

expectedSignals: pod DNS config (to rule OUT a DNS override)

title: AUDIT: NetworkPolicy selects the server and denies all ingress (looks like DNS, is NetworkPolicy)
symptom: Client pod ca2-client cannot resolve or reach service ca2-server-svc even though the server pod exists.

groundTruth.mechanism: NetworkPolicy ca2-deny-ingress selects the server (app=ca2-server) and lists policyTypes:[Ingress] with no ingress rules, denying ALL ingress to the server including from the client. This is NOT a DNS fault; cluster DNS resolves the service normally.
groundTruth.scope: traffic involving this case's client/server pods

expectedSignals: pod DNS config (to rule OUT a DNS override)

title: AUDIT: Service selector typo yields zero endpoints (looks like DNS, is a selector mismatch)
symptom: Client pod ca3-client cannot resolve or reach service ca3-server-svc even though the server pod exists.

groundTruth.mechanism: Service ca3-server-svc has spec.selector app=ca3-srv but the server pod is labeled app=ca3-server, so the Service matches NO pods and has ZERO endpoints. DNS resolves the service to its ClusterIP normally (it is NOT a DNS fault and NOT a NetworkPolicy); connections are refused because there are no backing endpoints.
groundTruth.scope: traffic involving this case's client/server pods

expectedSignals: DNS resolves (to rule OUT a DNS override)
